newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases financial service rules for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: India eases financial service rules for foreigners.

text.p: India on Tuesday revised equity levels for foreign investors in non-banking financial services (NBFCs), and spelled out minimum levels of investment pegged to the extent of foreign equity participation.

The Finance Ministry said in a statement that foreign investment would be permitted in a host of financial services including merchant banking, underwriting, portfolio management services, financial consultancy, stockbroking, asset management, venture capital firms, and credit rating agencies.

The statement said the minimum capitalisation would be $500,000 in NBFCs where foreign equity was 51 percent or less, $5.0 million in NBFCs where foreign equity was more than 51 percent but less than or equal to 75 percent, and $50 million in NBFCs where foreign equity was more than 75 percent.
It said 100 percent foreign-owned NBFCs would be required to act as holding companies, with specific activities undertaken by subsidiaries with a minimum domestic equity of 25 percent.
The ministry said for foreign equity holdings between 75 and 100 percent, capitalisation would need to be $7.5 million up-front with the balance to be brought in over 24 months.
For subsidiaries of 100 percent foreign-owned NBFCs, domestic equity amounting to 10 percent would have to be up-front with the balance domestic equity to be introduced over a period of 24 months.
